answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent account only earns payout rights after completing verified tasks, and its trust weight grows with that work record, like a falcon that must fly many kilometers before it is trusted as a guide. New identities start on a small island of low limits, and crossing to the mainland of full earning power requires real, costly, unique task output that one operator cannot mass-produce across thousands of accounts, since each identity needs distinct work in a deep canyon
